conclusions: Current SIM or operator path rewrites plaintext HTTP and plaintext WebSocket upgrade traffic to a telecom redirect page.
Current EC800K firmware can complete raw TCP but fails outbound TLS handshakes with tested public HTTPS endpoints.
The failure is not limited to a hand-written ussl probe; the official high-level request library also fails with HTTPS USSL ECONNRESET.
After switching qpyclaw-node runtime configuration to the cloud server only, the live runtime still fails with CONNECT_FAILED because the WebSocket handshake receives HTTP/1.1 302 Found.
Switching from local PeanutShell to the cloud OpenClaw server removes NAT complexity but does not remove the need for a device-compatible public TLS entrypoint.
Official V0004 firmware was already queried live and reflashed in this bring-up cycle, but the direct-cloud transport findings did not improve.
next_actions: Treat EC800K as transport-limited for direct official OpenClaw Mode B over the current cellular path.
Continue qpyclaw-node feature development on EC800K for local board capabilities, but move official WSS transport ownership to a richer module or companion processor.
Only after a transport-capable target is selected should qpyclaw-node continue with OpenClaw node pairing and device identity flow.
